messages:
Mike: paging — noticed sustained increase in batch build time + P95 token latency across prod cluster A (north-1). Spike started ~15:40 UTC, correlated with large proportion of long-seq requests from a single customer set. Seeing queue depth climb and batching window expand.

Jia: saw the alert, grabbing logs now. initial p95 for text generation up to 1.6s, some tails >3s. throughput still high but latency SLOs violated for many routes.

Mike: impact: a handful of mid-tier customers saw errors/timeouts, and some free-tier saw severe slowdowns. CS got ~4 escalations. tagging @CS-Alerts for heads-up.

CS-Alerts: acknowledged. we have two open tickets (T-4231, T-4232) from customers with real-time needs. We're letting them know we're on it.

Jia: hypothesis — continuous batching window auto-expanded because of increased variance in seq lengths, causing large batches that blow up end-to-end latency. Quick mitigation options: 1) shrink continuous batching window (ms) 2) cap max batch tokens 3) apply short-term rate limits for specific customer(s) 4) disable long-seq batching path.

Mike: prioritize latency over throughput for next 20–30m. I'll apply config changes. Tom — can you take over monitoring? I'm going offline for read-only for 10m.

Tom: on it. what's the exact change you want to roll? I can patch runtime config via the infra admin API.

Mike: plan: a) reduce continuous_window_ms from 80 -> 25 b) decrease max_batch_tokens 4096 -> 1024 c) enable latency_priority flag so runtime favors smaller batches d) add a temporary rate limit rule for customer-team X to 15rps. If anything worse, we fallback to disabling long-seq batching path.

Jia: add me to the patch. I'll tail logs for any increase in errors after change. Also will run a quick canary on a subset of hosts.

Mike: applying change now (running admin script). command:

```
curl -X POST https://infra-admin.internal/redwood/v1/runtime/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "batching": {
      "continuous_window_ms": 25,
      "max_batch_tokens": 1024,
      "latency_priority": true
    },
    "rate_limits": [{
      "customer_id": "cust-team-x",
      "limit_rps": 15,
      "duration_minutes": 60,
      "reason": "live mitigation - reduce tail latency"
    }]
  }'
```

SRE-Bot: config_change_event: user=Mike, scope=prod/north-1, change_id=cfg-9876, status=applied -> partial (rolling patch started)

Tom: patch rolled out to 30% hosts in north-1 canary pool. metrics look promising: p50 unaffected, p95 falling from 1600ms -> 420ms on canary. queue depth down ~40%.

Adele: quick note from CS — two customers asked about root cause. Can we provide a short blurb once we stabilise? They want ETA.

Jia: yes. will prepare a short incident blurb: "experiencing transient latency due to burst of long-sequence workloads; temporary batching window tightened and per-customer rate limit applied. Monitoring for regressions; will update in 30m." Sending to Adele after we confirm.

Mike: rolling to remainder of north-1 (expected 6 min). keeping long-seq path enabled for now but we have the toggle ready.

SRE-Bot: rollout progress: 30% -> 60% -> 100% (completed). change_id=cfg-9876

Tom: post-rollout numbers: p95 at the global route down to 430ms, error rate down to baseline. CPU usage up slightly on hosts (more small batches). cost/unit increased ~6% but acceptable for mitigation window.

Jia: ran synthetic traffic against edge to confirm correctness; no regression in output. Also checking KV cache hit rates — small drop but nothing alarming.

Mike: good. leaving a note for next oncall: we'll keep the rate limit and lower batching window for 1 hour, then reassess. If latency stays good, we can relax max_batch_tokens to 2048 and raise window to 40ms.

Tom: handoff to Tom for continued watch. I'm headed to lunch. @Tom please escalate to infra-alerts if p95 > 800ms again.

Tom: acknowledged. setting 5-min dashboard heartbeat and an automated alert: if p95 > 800ms for 3 consecutive windows, page eng-oncall.

SRE-Bot: alert_rule_created: id=alert-7552, threshold=p95>800ms, window=3x5m, notify_channel=eng-oncall

Adele: I'll send the CS blurb now to the two affected customers and update the existing tickets. copying the mitigation steps + ETA for rollback.

CS-Alerts: message sent to customers T-4231/T-4232. customers acknowledged, asked for a postmortem once incident resolved.

Tom: monitoring for 25 minutes so far, numbers stable. leaving this thread in the incident log. notes for follow-up: 1) consider tuning continuous_window default for long-seq heavy workloads 2) add per-customer adaptive throttling to avoid broad rate limits 3) add rate-limit exception workflow for enterprise customers.

Mike: thanks all. If Tom sees anything odd, @Mike will rejoin. otherwise will create a short incident summary and post in /incidents channel tomorrow.

Tom: copying my watch runbook into incident tracker. closing active mitigation; will keep rule active for 60m then auto-remove if stable.

SRE-Bot: incident_closed? mitigation_active=true; followup_task=INC-1029 (tune defaults + add adaptive throttling)

Adele: thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Mike: nice quick turn. :party_popper:
